newsitem.title: MAURITANIA: Mauritania frees three held over Libya links.
newsitem.headline: Mauritania frees three held over Libya links.

text.p: Mauritania has freed the head of the main opposition Action for Change party and two other politicians held on allegations of suspect relations with Libya, family and other sources close to them said on Thursday.
Messoud Ould Boulkheir, whose Action for Change party won the first and only opposition seat in October's parliamentary poll, was arrested with three other politicians on January 22.

The others were Abdallahi el Atigh Ould Yahi, spokesman for a group opposing normalisation with Israel, El Khory ould Hmeity, former general-secretary of the Mauritanian workers union, and Hamoud Ould Abdi, a member of the national committee of the ruling Democratic and Social Republican Party.

Boulkheir, who began a hunger strike on Tuesday, was released overnight Wednesday. Sources close to Hmeity and Abdi said they too had been released. No action appeared to have been taken against them, the sources said.
Political sources say a further six people remain in custody over the affair.
Mauritania's relations with Libya, shunned by the West on suspicion of terrorism links, are traditionally strained, with Nouakchott accusing Tripoli of trying to destabilise it.
President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya and his ruling party won a landslide victory in October's parliamentary election.

Action for Change is a new party championing the rights of Mauritania's blacks and ex-slaves. Moors of Arab stock traditionally dominate the government of the former French colony, which straddles black and Arab Africa.
